verdict.rationale: ROS 2 documents QoS settings for non-ideal networks, ranging from TCP-like reliable to UDP-like best-effort, plus predefined sensor-data profiles and topics for streaming sensor and robot status. A long-time user also reports that ROS gives you teleop 'for free' if you follow its conventions. Beyond that, the evidence shows no dedicated teleoperation tooling, live video streaming, or proven responsive remote control over WAN or cellular links, so most of the story rests on general pub/sub primitives. Missing for 10: documented first-party teleop tooling, live video streaming/compression over constrained links, latency or responsiveness evidence over real-world remote networks, independent hands-on corroboration of remote teleop.
